learningObjective: Predict how TorchInductor fuses a chain of pointwise ops on CUDA and how many kernels the compiled function produces.

canonicalClaims.claim: TorchInductor's scheduler fuses pointwise producer-consumer chains that share an iteration space into a single generated Triton kernel on CUDA, so intermediate tensors are not materialized in HBM.
conditions: All ops in the chain are pointwise with the same shape and layout.
There is no reduction, side-effecting op, unsupported op, or explicit `torch._dynamo.disable` in the chain.
Inputs live on the same CUDA device.
nonImplications: Does not imply that reductions never fuse — Inductor also fuses many reduction patterns with pointwise producers/epilogues, but only single-pass shapes.
Does not imply that the resulting kernel is optimal; the fused kernel is still memory-bound and won't approach compute peak.

misconceptions.claim: Pointwise ops with different scalar constants (e.g., `x*2` vs `x+1`) cannot be fused by TorchInductor.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Scalars are constants in the generated Triton code and do not affect the ability to share an iteration space.

misconceptions.claim: TorchInductor lowers CUDA tensors to CPU C++ code when in default mode.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Inductor selects a device-appropriate backend: Triton for CUDA, C++ for CPU.

misconceptions.claim: Every torch.compile call produces exactly one kernel per user-visible op.
misconceptions.whyWrong: The whole point of Inductor is to fuse; producing one kernel per op would defeat the compile step.

misconceptions.claim: A dedicated materialization kernel is emitted at the end of every fused chain to place the result into the output tensor.
misconceptions.whyWrong: The fused kernel writes directly to the output buffer; no separate materialization launch is required.

implementationFacts: Inductor supports Triton codegen (CUDA) and C++ codegen (CPU)
Pointwise fusion is the most common Inductor pattern; producer-consumer with matching iteration space fuses by default
Reduction fusion requires that the reduction fits the fusion pattern (single reduction dim, matching output shape)
performanceScenarios: Fusing a chain of pointwise activations avoids intermediate HBM traffic, which is the dominant win for memory-bound kernels.
